subject: FinServCo-prod: sudden error surge & peering/DNS anomalies — immediate support
messages:
From: Lisa Mendez <lisa.mendez@finserv.example.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-21T09:12:00Z
Subject: Urgent - production error surge and timeouts (FinServCo prod)

Aditya / Marissa —

We're seeing a rapid increase in 5xx and 429 responses from the dedicated cluster serving FinServCo-prod starting ~08:50 UTC. Customer-facing latency has spiked and several settlement jobs are timing out. Attached is a short CSV with counts by status code for the last hour and a few example request IDs.

Key impact:
- 5xx rate up from ~0.3% to 6.8%
- 429 rate up to ~12% during peak windows
- Throughput dropped ~40% for the main tenant shard

We opened this with our SREs but wanted Redwood on this immediately — this is blocking settlement processing (batch jobs) and our ops manager has asked for a P0.

We think this may be related to networking between our VPC and the dedicated nodes (we saw intermittent TCP resets and some DNS lookup failures for inference endpoints). Can you confirm you have a plan and ETA for mitigation?

Attachments: [attachment: error_summary.csv (CSV)]

Lisa
Lisa Mendez
Head of Platform Ops, FinServCo

Subject: Re: Urgent - production error surge and timeouts (FinServCo prod)

Lisa — thank you for the heads-up and the data. We're treating this as P0. I've looped in our infra lead (Jonas) and CS lead (Marissa). Jonas — can you confirm whether this looks like a networking / peering issue or something internal on our runtime?

Immediate plan:
- Jonas to triage network layer and report back within 30 minutes
- If we can identify a short traffic-steering mitigation we will propose it (regional fallback or temporary traffic split)
- We'll provide a customer-facing timeline and next steps within 1 hour

Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
T: +1 415 555 0107
From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-21T09:46:00Z
Subject: Re: Urgent - production error surge and timeouts (FinServCo prod)

TL;DR: Early signals point to peering route instability + DNS TTL drift affecting NAT translation and causing a burst of connection resets and SYN retries.

What I've observed so far (quick notes):
- BGP route churn on our peering session to the customer's transit at ~08:48—08:52 UTC (route flap counters spike).
- Several dedicated nodes reported connection resets and TCP retransmit escalations; correlate with the same times as the customer's 5xx/429 spike.
- DNS cache on a subset of edge routers shows TTLs unexpectedly low (several A records caching <5s), amplifying lookups under load.
- NAT SNAT port usage for that peering block is near exhaustion for a short-lived burst; we see retransmits when ephemeral ports are unavailable.

Immediate mitigations I'm pushing now:
1) Increase DNS TTL caching on edge for the affected model endpoints to 30s temporarily (to reduce query amplification).
2) Expand SNAT ephemeral port allocation for the affected egress path; roll this out to the cluster in 2 waves (10 nodes each) — low-risk.
3) Opened a peering ticket with our cloud partner (ticket #CP-14892) to investigate the route churn.

Attachments: [attachment: diagnostic-snapshot.txt]

I'll update in 30 minutes with telemetry and whether the mitigation reduced 429s.

— Jonas
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Mendez <lisa.mendez@finserv.example.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-21T10:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Urgent - production error surge and timeouts (FinServCo prod)

Lisa — thank you for staying on this. Quick customer update from our side:

What we have done (10:00–10:15 UTC):
- Applied temporary DNS caching increase on edge nodes (aim: reduce query amplification).
- Expanded SNAT pool for the affected egress path; we validated allocation on canary nodes.
- Enabled short-term traffic steering: 15% of traffic shifted to a nearby healthy region to relieve pressure on the peering path.

Observed effect (10:05–10:15 UTC):
- 429s dropped from 12% to ~4% on the canary shard; 5xxs trending down but still elevated (~2.1%).

Next steps / asks:
- We're coordinating with cloud partner for the peering BGP churn RCA (Jonas is owning).
- We will run a full route-dump and share with your network team (sending link shortly).
- If you approve, we'll keep the traffic steering and SNAT expansion for the next 6 hours while the partner investigates.

Marissa Cole
Customer Success, Redwood Inference

- We need a written timeline for the full RCA and permanent fix (this impacts our settlement SLAs).
- Please capture whether this was strictly a peering issue vs any Redwood config change. Our legal/ops team is asking about potential SLA credits if the root cause is on the provider side.
- Sharing a short snippet of our telemetry: we also saw DNS query spikes from internal batch runners right before the window; attaching a small route dump we captured.

Attachments: [attachment: peering-route-dump.json]

Lisa

Date: 2027-08-21T16:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Urgent - production error surge and timeouts (FinServCo prod)

Lisa — appreciate the route dump. High level next steps and commitments from Redwood: 

1) RCA & timeline: Jonas is coordinating with our cloud partner and will produce an interim RCA within 24 hours and a full RCA within 72 hours. If the RCA attributes root cause to our routing or config, we will document remediation and a credit calculation for SLA impact.

2) Short-term support: We will retain the temporary SNAT expansion and traffic steering for the next 6–12 hours and monitor. If you'd like, we can extend that window until your peak processing completes — please confirm.

3) Permanent remediation: If route churn is recurring we will work with the partner to set up a dedicated backup path and stronger BGP dampening; we will run a controlled exercise to validate TTL and SNAT headroom.

4) Executive signal: Vivek is on this thread for exec visibility; if FinServCo wants an executive briefing we can schedule 30m with our GM by EOD tomorrow.

I'll keep you posted with telemetry updates and the interim RCA. Thank you for your patience and collaboration.

— Aditya
Enterprise Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
